learn.hook: Let us go to the market! First, let us know our money.
points: Our money is the rupee. We write ₹.
Coins are round and made of metal: ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10.
Notes are made of paper: ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100.
A ₹5 coin is worth five ₹1 coins.
learn.reallife: We pay with coins and notes at the sabzi market and the sweet shop.

games.title: Smallest to biggest
games.prompt: Put money in order, least first

quiz.q: Which is worth the most?
quiz.explain: 5 is more than 2 and 1. So ₹5 is worth the most.
steps: 5 is more than 2 and more than 1.
So the ₹5 coin is worth the most.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger-looking coin is worth more

quiz.q: How many ₹1 coins make ₹2?
quiz.mistake: Thinks one coin of any kind is the same

quiz.q: Which one is a note, not a coin?
quiz.explain: ₹100 comes as a paper note. ₹1 and ₹2 are coins.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which money is paper

quiz.q: Riya has two ₹5 coins. How much money is that?
quiz.mistake: Writes 5 and 5 together

quiz.q: How many ₹10 notes make ₹20?
quiz.explain: ₹10 + ₹10 = ₹20. That is 2 notes.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the value with the number of notes

quiz.q: What sign do we use for rupees?
quiz.explain: ₹ is the sign for our rupee.
steps: $ is not our sign. + means add.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up money signs

teach.ask: Gappu: My shiny coin and a paper note. Which is money?
teach.praise: Both! Coins and notes are both rupees. Wow!
teach.nudge: Are coins money? Are notes money too? What do we call our money?

revise.summary: Our money is the rupee, written ₹. Coins are round and made of metal, and notes are made of paper.
focus: Find how many smaller coins or notes make an amount
Say which coin is worth the most
remember: Our money is the rupee. We write ₹.
Coins are round and made of metal: ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10.
A ₹5 coin is worth five ₹1 coins.
traps: A bigger-looking coin is not always worth more.
Don't mix up the value with the number of notes.
Two ₹5 coins make ₹10. Don't write 5 and 5 together.

learn.hook: Rahim Kaka sells toys! Do you have enough money?
points: Rahim Kaka's toys have price tags: a whistle ₹5, a ball ₹10, a doll ₹14.
Four ₹5 coins make ₹20: 5, 10, 15, 20.
Two ₹10 notes make ₹20.
If a toy costs ₹14 and you have ₹10, you need ₹4 more.
With ₹30, pick toys whose prices add up to ₹30 or less.

example.q: A doll costs ₹14. Sara has ₹10. How much more does she need?

learn.reallife: At a mela, we check our money before choosing a toy.

items.text: Toy ₹14, I have ₹10. I need ₹___ more.
Toy ₹18, I have ₹10. I need ₹___ more.

games.title: True or false?
items: Two ₹10 notes make ₹20.
Three ₹5 coins make ₹20.
5, 10, 15. Three make only ₹15.
With ₹30 you can buy a ₹10 ball and a ₹20 kite.
With ₹30 you can buy a ₹20 kite and a ₹15 drum.
20 + 15 = 35. That is more than ₹30.

quiz.q: How many ₹5 coins make ₹20?
quiz.explain: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 coins.
quiz.mistake: Stops at ₹15

quiz.q: A kite costs ₹20. Ravi pays only with ₹10 notes. How many notes does he give?
steps: The kite costs ₹20. He uses ₹10 notes.
quiz.mistake: Gives one note

quiz.q: A toy car costs ₹17. Sara has ₹10. How much more does she need?
quiz.explain: Count up from 10 to 17: that is ₹7.
steps: Count up from 10 to 17: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17. That is 7.
quiz.mistake: Adds the price and the money

quiz.q: A drum costs ₹19. Kabir has ₹15. How much more does he need?
quiz.explain: 15 + 4 = 19. He needs ₹4 more.
steps: Count up from 15 to 19: 16, 17, 18, 19. That is 4.
quiz.mistake: Counts one too many

quiz.q: Meena and Aisha have ₹30 together. Which two toys can they buy?
quiz.explain: 10 + 20 = 30. The others cost ₹35 and ₹33, too much.
quiz.mistake: Does not add the two prices

quiz.q: Ball ₹10, whistle ₹5, top ₹12. You have ₹30. Can you buy all three?
quiz.explain: 10 + 5 + 12 = 27. That is less than 30.
steps: 27 is less than 30. So yes, they cost ₹27 in all.
Answer: Yes, they cost ₹27 in all
quiz.mistake: Does not add all three prices

teach.ask: Gappu: A toy costs ₹15. I have ₹10. Can I buy it? How much more do I need?
teach.praise: Not yet! You need ₹5 more. Save up, Gappu!
teach.nudge: Is ₹10 as much as ₹15? Count up from 10 to 15.

revise.summary: Rahim Kaka's toys have price tags. Count up to find how much more money you need, and add prices to see what you can buy.
focus: Find how many coins or notes make a price
Find how much more money is needed by counting up
Add prices to see if you can buy them
remember: If a toy costs ₹14 and you have ₹10, you need ₹4 more.
With ₹30, pick toys whose prices add up to ₹30 or less.
traps: Don't add the price and the money when finding how much more.
Add all the prices before deciding.
Don't stop at ₹15 when counting ₹5 coins to ₹20.

learn.hook: At the mela, toys have prices. Can we buy them?
points: The price tells how much a thing costs.
If we have enough money, we can buy it.
If we pay more, we get some money back. That is change.
Change = money given - price.

example.q: A balloon costs ₹7. Riya pays ₹10. How much change?

learn.reallife: At the sweet shop, the shopkeeper gives back change when we pay more.

games.title: True or false?
items: With ₹10, Arjun can buy a ₹8 toy.
₹10 is more than ₹8.
With ₹5, Meena can buy a ₹9 book.
₹5 is less than ₹9. Not enough money.
Pay ₹10 for a ₹4 ball. Change is ₹6.
Pay ₹20 for a ₹12 cap. Change is ₹12.
If you pay the exact price, you get no change.
Nothing is left over.

quiz.q: A pencil costs ₹5. Kabir pays ₹10. How much change?
quiz.mistake: Adds the price to the money paid

quiz.q: A laddoo costs ₹8. Aisha has ₹6. Can she buy it?
quiz.explain: ₹6 is less than ₹8. She needs ₹2 more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any money is enough

quiz.q: A toy car costs ₹13. Joseph pays ₹20. How much change?
quiz.explain: Count up from 13 to 20: that is 7.
quiz.mistake: Counts on one extra

quiz.q: Riya buys a ₹4 eraser and a ₹5 pencil. How much does she spend?
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding

quiz.q: Riya pays ₹10 for things worth ₹9. How much change?
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of taking away

quiz.q: Arjun has ₹15. Which can he buy?
quiz.explain: ₹12 is less than ₹15. The others cost more than he has.
steps: ₹12 is less than ₹15. So he can buy the ₹12 top.
quiz.mistake: Picks a price higher than his money

teach.ask: Gappu: The kite costs ₹6. I gave ₹10. Why did I get money back?
teach.praise: I paid more than the price, so I get ₹4 change!
teach.nudge: Did I pay more than the price? How do I find the change?

revise.summary: The price tells how much a thing costs. If we pay more, we get money back, called change, and change is money given minus the price.
focus: Find the change by counting up or taking away
Say if you have enough money to buy something
Add two prices to find what you spend
remember: If we pay more, we get some money back. That is change.
traps: Don't add the price to the money paid.
Not every amount is enough. Check it is not less than the price.

learn.hook: Arjun has a few coins. How much money does he have?
points: Add the value of each coin or note.
Start with the biggest one. Count on.
Different coins can make the same amount.

example.q: Meena has a ₹10 coin, a ₹5 coin and a ₹2 coin. How much in all?

learn.reallife: We count money in our piggy bank. Shopkeepers count the money we give.

quiz.q: Kabir has ₹10 and ₹2. How much in all?
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding

quiz.q: Aisha has three ₹2 coins. How much money?
quiz.mistake: Counts the coins, not their value

quiz.q: Which makes ₹10?
quiz.mistake: Adds wrongly

quiz.q: Harpreet has a ₹10 note, a ₹5 coin and a ₹1 coin. How much?
quiz.mistake: Forgets one coin

quiz.q: Joseph has ₹20 and Riya has ₹10. How much together?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts instead of adding

quiz.q: Meena has 4 coins: ₹5, ₹5, ₹2, ₹1. How much?
quiz.mistake: Counts the coins instead of adding their values

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 3 coins. So I have ₹3, right?
teach.praise: Oh! Each coin has its own value. I must add them up!
teach.nudge: Is every coin worth ₹1? What should I add?

revise.summary: To add money, add the value of each coin or note. Start with the biggest one and count on.
focus: Add coins and notes by their value
Start with the biggest coin or note
Know different coins can make the same amount
remember: Add the value of each coin or note.
Start with the biggest one. Count on.
Different coins can make the same amount.
traps: Count the value, not the number of coins.
Don't take away when adding money.

learn.hook: Can 1 coin do the work of 5 coins? Yes! Let us see how.
points: ₹10 can be one ₹10 coin, two ₹5 coins or five ₹2 coins.
To use the fewest coins, start with the biggest coin that fits.
₹7 with the fewest coins: ₹5 + ₹2. That is 2 coins.
Two groups match if they have the same total, even with different coins.

example.q: Make ₹8 with the fewest coins. You have ₹1, ₹2, ₹5 and ₹10 coins.
steps: ₹10 is too big. Take ₹5. ₹3 is left.

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers give change with the fewest coins so their coin box does not run out.

quiz.q: What is the fewest number of coins that make ₹10?
quiz.explain: One ₹10 coin is enough.
steps: Fewest coins means use the biggest coin that fits.
quiz.mistake: Uses smaller coins when one big coin fits

quiz.q: Make ₹9 with the fewest coins (₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10). How many coins?
quiz.explain: ₹5 + ₹2 + ₹2 = ₹9. That is 3 coins.
quiz.mistake: Uses only ₹1 coins

quiz.q: Which group has the same value as ₹10?
quiz.mistake: Counts coins instead of adding their values

quiz.q: Riya has ₹5 + ₹5 + ₹5. Kabir has ₹10 + ₹5. What is true?
quiz.mistake: Thinks more coins means more money

quiz.q: Make ₹12 with the fewest coins (₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10). How many coins?
quiz.explain: ₹10 + ₹2 = ₹12. Just 2 coins.
quiz.mistake: Does not start with the biggest coin

quiz.q: Which matches a ₹20 note?
steps: Two ₹5 coins are ₹10. One ₹10 coin is ₹10.
quiz.mistake: Does not add the values

teach.ask: Gappu: I want to carry ₹6 with as few coins as I can. Which coins should I take?
teach.nudge: Which is the biggest coin that fits in ₹6?

revise.summary: The same amount can be made with different coins. To use the fewest coins, start with the biggest coin that fits.
focus: Make an amount with the fewest coins
Find groups of coins with the same value
Know more coins does not mean more money
remember: ₹10 can be one ₹10 coin, two ₹5 coins or five ₹2 coins.
To use the fewest coins, start with the biggest coin that fits.
₹7 with the fewest coins: ₹5 + ₹2. That is 2 coins.
traps: More coins does not mean more money.
Don't use small coins when one big coin fits.
Add the values, don't count the coins.

learn.hook: Clink! Clink! Coins go into the piggy bank. Let us save!
points: Saving means keeping some money for later.
A piggy bank keeps our coins safe.
Add each coin you put in to know how much you have saved.
Saving a little every day adds up to a lot!

example.q: Monday ₹5, Tuesday ₹2, Wednesday ₹2 go in the piggy bank. How much is saved?

learn.reallife: Many children save coins for a book, a toy or a gift for someone they love.

games.title: True or false?
items: Saving money is a good habit.
It helps us buy things we need later.
A piggy bank keeps coins safe.
Coins stay inside until we need them.
If we save ₹1 a day for 5 days, we save ₹5.
We should spend all our money at once.
Saving some helps us buy bigger things later.

quiz.q: Joseph puts ₹2, ₹5 and ₹1 in his piggy bank. How much has he saved?
quiz.mistake: Misses a coin

quiz.q: Riya saves ₹2 every day for 5 days. How much does she save?
steps: Riya saves ₹2 each day for 5 days.
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 and 5

quiz.q: Why do we save money?
options: To buy something we need later
quiz.explain: Saved money can be used later for something useful.
steps: So we save to buy something we need later.
Answer: To buy something we need later
quiz.mistake: Does not know why saving helps

quiz.q: Kabir's piggy bank has ₹10 + ₹10 + ₹5. How much is in it?
quiz.mistake: Misses the ₹5 coin

quiz.q: Aisha wants a ₹20 book. She has saved ₹15. How much more must she save?
steps: Count up from 15 to 20: 16, 17, 18, 19, 20. That is 5.
quiz.mistake: Adds the price and the savings

quiz.q: Which is a good saving habit?
options: Put a coin in the piggy bank each week
quiz.explain: Saving a little often adds up.
steps: Spending all or throwing coins away leaves nothing.
A coin in the piggy bank each week adds up.
So that is a good saving habit.
Answer: Put a coin in the piggy bank each week
quiz.mistake: Does not see what saving means

teach.ask: Gappu: Why should I put my coins in a piggy bank? How do I know how much I saved?
teach.praise: Saving keeps coins safe for later. Add them up to know your total!
teach.nudge: What is a piggy bank for? How do I find the total?

revise.summary: Saving means keeping some money for later, and a piggy bank keeps our coins safe. Add each coin you put in to know how much you have saved.
focus: Add the coins put in a piggy bank
Find how much more to save for something
remember: Saving means keeping some money for later.
Add each coin you put in to know how much you have saved.
Saving a little every day adds up to a lot!
traps: Don't add the price and the savings when finding how much more.
₹2 for 5 days is ₹10. Don't add 2 and 5.
